title: Critique: consciousness may need a living, self-maintaining body or a specific material

statements.text: A proposed necessary condition is that conscious systems be autopoietic, sustaining their own existence and organization as living things do. Godfrey-Smith argues that self-maintenance depends on how molecules behave at the nanometer scale in water, so artificial systems can bear only coarse-grained functional similarity to organisms, which will not suffice for consciousness. If a noncomputational feature of living organisms is necessary, consciousness is impossible in nonorganic systems.
